verdict.rationale: The evidence shows Codex CalculateTokenUsage was written to scan the whole rollout and use cumulative total_token_usage, with a later fix adding a baseline delta. Nothing in it shows that reparsing the full transcript every turn was chosen over incremental slicing; the performance consequence was never discussed.

Funnel all session-state mutations through MutateSessionState

The previous PostToolUse-only lock fixed parallel PostToolUse races but
left every other writer (TurnEnd, PostCommit, condense, model update,
review env adoption, attribution divergence, post-rewrite remap, etc.)
doing its own unlocked load → mutate → save. A PostToolUse save could
still revert Phase, CheckpointTranscriptStart, TurnCheckpointIDs, token
usage, and other fields if it landed between another writer's load and
save.

Convert every session-state load-modify-save in the lifecycle dispatcher
and strategy package to MutateSessionState (or, for the rare new-state
case, to wrap the lone save in acquireSessionGate). The helper now:
  - Takes an OS flock against .git/entire-session-locks/<id>.lock for
    the duration of the load + fn + save.
  - Layers a per-process gate keyed by goroutine ID over the flock so
    nested calls in the same goroutine share the outer's state pointer
    rather than deadlocking on a second flock or losing inner updates
    to the outer save.
  - Returns ErrStateNotFound when no state file exists, letting callers
    distinguish "no session" from a successful no-op.
  - Honours ErrMutationSkip so fn can decline to save when the merge
    produced no change (key for the PostToolUse hot path).

Lock files moved out of .git/entire-sessions/ so callers that enumerate
session state (tests, doctor, status) don't have to filter them.
ClearSessionState sweeps the lock too.

Adds TestMutat

fix(claudecode): use bufio.Reader to handle arbitrarily long transcript lines

Replace bufio.Scanner with bufio.Reader.ReadBytes to remove the 10MB line
size limit in GetTranscriptPosition and ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset.

Scanner fails with "token too long" when transcript lines exceed its buffer
size, which can happen with large tool outputs. ReadBytes has no artificial
limit and will allocate as needed.

sanitized transcript copy under .entire/metadata/<session>/ stays as
before and is what condensation reads when the live transcript is gone.
